posts.title: The Instruments of Darkness by John Connolly
posts.description: As it happens, I have read the first twenty books in this series — this is number 21 in Connolly’s Charlie Parker series. Unlike the classic Parker books by Richard Stark (which I finished reading through for a second time this year) these are relatively thick and occasionally a little dense. posts.title: Enter Night by Mick Wall
posts.description: Much of what I wrote about Never Enough applies here in terms of the approach of music journalists. posts.title: Never Enough by Jeff Apter
posts.description: I am old enough to remember when The Cure were releasing some of their more famous singles and albums and I did spend a lot of time listening to them in my late teens. They were never my favourite but, like many of the bands from that time, they’ve been ever-present and my enjoyment of them has grown.
